L514@P7: instance, 2, 000 candidate trajectories × 10 timesteps per
L515@P7: trajectory is well aligned with the literature [3, 29–31, 43].
L516@P7: With 200, 000 trajectories, this allows for 10 queries per
L517@P7: timestep to integrate occupancy over the volume of the SDV,
L518@P7: which should provide a good estimation of collision probability. We notice that for ≲ 20, 000 query points, IMPLICITO has a constant inference time because it is batched over
L519@P7: query points. Once the GPU is saturated, the operations are
L520@P7: run sequentially so inference time increases approximately
L521@P7: linearly. The explicit decoders have approximately constant
L522@P7: inference times (the only increase is due to bilinear interpolation), but are significantly slower than IMPLICITO in this
L523@P7: “planner-relevant” range.
L524@P7: 5. Conclusion
L525@P7: In this paper, we have proposed a unified approach to
L526@P7: joint perception and prediction for self-driving that implicitly represents occupancy and flow over time with a neural
L527@P7: network. This queryable implicit representation can provide
L528@P7: information to a downstream motion planner more effectively and efficiently. We showcased that our implicit architecture predicts occupancy and flow more accurately than
L529@P7: contemporary explicit approaches in both urban and highway settings. Further, this approach outperforms more traditional object-based perception and prediction paradigms.
L530@P7-8: In the future, we plan to assess the impact of our improvements on the downstream task of motion planning.References

L274@P4: Datasets: We conduct our experiments using two
L275@P4: datasets: Argoverse 2 Sensor [40] (urban), and HighwaySim (highway). The Argoverse 2 Sensor (AV2) dataset
L276@P4: is collected in U.S. cities and consists of 850 fifteen-second

L288@P4: boxes. Occupied query points are labeled with flow vectors using finite differences between the current query point

L392@P3: G. Recovering Agent IDs Using Flow Traces
L393@P3: The flow traces discussed as a loss in Sec. III-F.1 can also
L394@P3: be used at inference time to assign agent IDs to predicted
L395@P3: occupancies. If we augment the current occupancy grid O0
L396@P3: with the ID of the origin agent for every grid cell, the warping
L397@P3: process spreads the agent ID across the flow vectors as well.
L398@P3: In this setup, Wt contains flow-warped occupancies with percell ID attributes, from which we can directly read the agent
L399@P3: ID. This ID points to the agent that could occupy this grid
L400@P3: cell at time t according to the flow predictions F1, . . . , Ft.
L401@P3: Construction of flow traces and thereby the ID recovery
L402@P3: process is very fast with time complexity O(h · w · Tpred).
